planner_findings.title: AC8 cannot fail: step 1b's expectedStepCol pin is unreachable on MUT-Q
planner_findings.detail: Under the RATIFIED shallowest anchor, MUT-Q's derivation captures the OTHER JOB's `steps:` key (Declared Residual 8) and returns stepCol=6, which EQUALS expectedStepCol=6, so the pin's inequality branch is never taken. Measured on the locator prototype: MUT-Q with step 1b -> FATAL via Invariant A, block [96,99); MUT-Q with step 1b NEUTERED -> FATAL via Invariant A, block [96,99). No flip. Both halves of AC8 pass identically in a build with step 1b and in a build without it. AC8's own neuter arm concedes this ('must still red via Invariant A or B'). By the mission's own MUT-N rule this is a grep in disguise.
planner_findings.resolution: AC8 replaced by AC8' built on new arm MUT-R (both job bodies re-indented two columns right): pin fires (stepCol=8 != 6), and with 1b neutered the same mutant is rc=0 GREEN. That rc=1 -> rc=0 flip is the liveness proof AC8 lacked. MUT-Q retained as AC8'-b, honestly relabelled as proving Invariant A / Residual 8 rather than the pin.

planner_findings.title: The MUT-Q row's landed-assertion is FALSE: the mutant the doc pins does not parse to 10 steps
planner_findings.detail: The MUT-Q row says 'assert LANDED by sha-differs from aed8e186... and by the ruby view still parsing to 10 steps.' The mutant that reproduces the doc's own pinned V31 sha 4fd378c4... yields `ailang-verify: steps=7` and `go-verify: steps=NIL`. Shifting only the `steps:` block two columns right moves the key from indent 4 (a job key) to indent 6, where it becomes a member of the `env:` mapping. features.name: Rewrite the locator, including Mechanism step 1b
features.description: Inside TestMiscompileInstrumentStepIsGatedInCI in host/verifygate/toolchain_pin_gate_test.go ONLY (func at :492; the two offending HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(...), "- name:") scans at :511 and :524). Add `indentOf` helper; `const miscompileStepName`; `const expectedStepCol = 6`. Step 1: derive stepCol from the SHALLOWEST enclosing `steps:` above i, tie broken at the minimal indent toward the nearest such line (a total rule); stepCol = indent of the first following line with trimmed prefix `- `; either lookup failing is a t.Fatalf("instrument failure: ..."). Step 1b: immediately after, `if stepCol != expectedStepCol { t.Fatalf("instrument failure: derived step column %d; update expectedStepCol after an intentional ci.yml re-indent", stepCol) }`. Step 2: start walks back from j := i INCLUSIVE to the nearest line with trimmed prefix `- ` AND indent exactly stepCol. Step 3: end from start+1 is the first dash line at exactly stepCol, or the first non-blank non-comment line at indent strictly less than stepCol, else EOF; blank and `#` lines never terminate. Invariant A: start <= i < end else t.Fatalf. Invariant B: the block must contain a line whose trimmed text is exactly "- name: "+miscompileStepName or "name: "+miscompileStepName, else t.Fatalf. The existing continue-on-error loop over [start,end) and everything after it is UNCHANGED. Update the function doc-comment: the DECLARED RESIDUAL block's scoping sentence and its reference to the ROW-44 doc's V19 now describe the new mechanism, and the comment names ruling D-WORLD-30. CORRECTS the design doc's MS1, which omits step 1b entirely (planner finding F3).
